requirement_text.REQ-364:
Implements REQ-363's design artefact exactly — no new schema decisions here, this requirement is implementation of an already-validated design, matching this project's own CODE-DESIGNER-then-ELIXIR-DEV split for every other schema-bearing feature.

SCOPE: the `Letflow.Help` context module (naming follows this project's existing per-domain-context convention, e.g. `Letflow.Identity`, `Letflow.TenantProvisioning`) exposing: create a draft, update a draft, publish (draft -> live, sets confirmed_at), re-confirm (bumps confirmed_at on an already-live row without changing body — the explicit "I checked this, it's still accurate" action), and read (by screen_id + tenant prefix, or by process_definition_id). Every write path enforces REQ-363's sanitization rule from that design, not a weakened version of it.

NOT IN SCOPE: the tenant-facing authoring UI (REQ-365 for platform, a separate future requirement for the tenant admin UI itself — this requirement's acceptance criteria stop at a working, tested context module, callable from IEx/tests, not yet wired to any HTTP route or frontend component). Route/controller wiring, if this project's own API-surface convention wants a separate requirement for it (matching the pattern most REQ-027..030-style definition CRUD work already used), is a natural fast-follow, not bundled here — state explicitly in this requirement's close-out whether a route was added or deliberately deferred, rather than leaving it ambiguous.

task.description: SECURITY-REVIEWER's rework-1 gate escalated a design-approach question (step-03b-security-reviewer-rework1.json): two rounds of the same bug class -- a regex denylist missing a valid CommonMark link-destination syntax variant -- were found against help_content.ex's write-path sanitizer. Determine whether the regex-denylist approach (design section 5.3 option 1) is sound but incomplete, or structurally unsound, and if the latter, name the concrete alternative (option 2: a real parser/AST-based sanitizer) and the concrete next routing step.
acceptance_criteria: A definitive verdict: is the regex-denylist approach sound-but-incomplete or structurally unsound
If structurally unsound, name a specific real library/mechanism to route CODE-DESIGNER toward, not just 'reconsider'
State the concrete next routing step (which agent, which artefact to amend) rather than leaving it open-ended

result.summary:
RECONSTRUCTION NOTE: this handoff was originally written live during WF02-REQ364-20260917's security-review saga as ad-hoc, non-schema JSON (informal top-level keys such as req/at/result-as-bare-string instead of HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md §2's real schema), the exact anti-pattern this session's own ISS-0692 precedent names. It has been rewritten into full schema conformance by a later ORCH session under §4.1's not_agent_attested mechanism. created_at/started_at/completed_at are all set to the file's own git-introducing-commit timestamp (`git log --follow --diff-filter=A --format=%aI --reverse -- <path>`), the best-available real timestamp, NOT the original live dispatch/claim/completion times, which were never recorded in schema-legal fields on disk. All findings, quoted test counts, and verification detail below are migrated verbatim in substance from the original ad-hoc file; nothing was invented or paraphrased away.

VERDICT: Regex denylist approach is structurally unsound, not incomplete. Two confirmed bypasses (reference-style links, angle-bracket-wrapped URLs) plus three more constructible without changing the threat model (backslash-escaping, HTML entity encoding, embedded whitespace/control characters per the OWASP javascript: URI filter bypass cheat sheet) -- all stem from the same root cause: the regex scans raw source bytes for a scheme: substring, but CommonMark link-destination resolution (and any real renderer) applies escape processing, entity decoding, and whitespace normalization the regex never implements.

CONCRETE NEXT STEP: Route back through CODE-DESIGNER to amend lib/letflow/design/req363-help-content-data-model.md section 5.3, resolving OQ-4: pick and name an actual library (e.g. html_sanitize_ex, or a CommonMark parser such as earmark/md feeding an AST-level link/image destination scheme check), specify the write-path mechanism precisely (parse -> walk link/image destination nodes -> reject on disallowed scheme, not strip-and-hope). New dependency requires REVIEWER sign-off on the specific choice, same procedural weight as REQ-356's PDF library precedent. Then back to ELIXIR-DEV to implement against the revised design. NOT a third ELIXIR-DEV regex patch round -- explicitly declined.

no_markdown_sanitization_dep_currently_in_tree: confirmed via full mix.exs deps/0 read -- ecto_sql, postgrex, plug, bandit, jason, telemetry, stream_data, yaml_elixir, ueberauth_oidcc, lua, wasmex, a PDF renderer, nothing markdown/sanitization-related.

issues.description: The regex-denylist write-path sanitizer (design section 5.3 option 1) is structurally unsound: it scans raw source bytes for a scheme: substring while CommonMark link-destination resolution applies escape processing, entity decoding, and whitespace normalization the regex never implements -- at least 5 distinct bypass classes are constructible against the same root cause.

result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER to amend req363-help-content-data-model.md section 5.3 resolving OQ-4 toward option (b) -- a real parser/AST-based sanitizer -- then to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR, then back to ELIXIR-DEV. Do not dispatch a third regex-patch rework round.
